title: Architecture Evolves
lines: The first architecture isn't the final architecture.

title: Don't Overengineer
lines: Today's complexity rarely needs tomorrow's architecture.

title: Think in Iterations
lines: Split everything into the smallest deliverable iteration.

title: Every Iteration Needs an Exit Condition
lines: Know when the iteration is complete.

title: Freeze Scope
lines: Don't add features halfway through an iteration.

title: Validate First
lines: Never let invalid data reach business logic.

title: Business Logic Doesn't Belong in Routes
Every API Needs One Purpose
lines: Avoid endpoints that do too many things.

title: The Architecture Spectrum
lines: Monolith: A single codebase deployed as one unit. Simple to build, but tightly coupled and harder to scale as teams grow.
Modular Monolith: Still one deployment unit, but strictly separated into independent logical modules. The best of both worlds for most projects.
Monorepo: A single version-controlled repository that holds multiple distinct projects or services. Simplifies dependency management and code sharing.
Microservices: Independently deployable services communicating over a network. Infinite scalability, but introduces heavy operational complexity.

title: Pre-Flight Security & Stability Checklist
lines: Input Validation: Sanitize all incoming data to strictly prevent SQL injection and XSS attacks.
Tenant Isolation: Lock users to their own ID. Enforce strict boundaries so users can never access another user's data.
CORS Configuration: Strictly configure CORS to block unauthorized external domains from making API calls.
Rate Limiting: Implement robust rate limiting to prevent spam and protect against DDoS attacks.
Observability: Always implement logging and monitoring to catch production crashes early and fix them immediately.

title: Graphify
lines: A tool designed to drastically reduce token usage in Agentic IDEs.
It works by creating a graph based on the context of the project to optimize how code is fed to the agent.
Seems really interesting, looking forward to trying it out soon.

title: Google AI Studio
lines: Need to explore the potential of Google's AI tools more deeply.
It provides really cool features like building entire Android apps and defining robust agents.
Google's rapid evolution in the AI space continues to be surprising and highly impressive.

title: Mastering cURL
lines: I want to learn and master using cURL with simple 2-3 word commands.
It acts just like Postman but directly in the terminal.
Perfect for testing APIs, checking links, handling file uploads, and more.

title: Agent Swarms: Reflo & Hermes
lines: Discovered 'reflo' and 'hermes' on GitHub, which are properly defined swarms of agents.
Really excited to use them, though they seem to require higher token limits to operate effectively.
They are definitely on my checklist to explore and try out soon.

title: The Huge Boom in MCPs
lines: There is a massive boom right now in Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
MCPs keep popping up for virtually all platforms, even extending to design sites.
Really looking forward to trying out specific ones like the Zerodha MCP and Firebase MCP.

title: Playwright
lines: I was looking for a way to test complete flows from a client's perspective, which led me to Playwright.
It became one of the best discoveries during the development of ShepherEd.
You can script complex user flows and it tests them perfectly, providing detailed reports and screenshots on failure.
It can even provide a full video recording of the test flow if requested. A genuinely incredible tool.

title: Resend
lines: One of the most resourceful tools for a developer when building a SaaS.
Incredibly easy to send professional emails, including rich HTML templates.
Offers an amazing free tier of 100 emails a day (3k/month). A truly cool and essential tool.

title: Cloudflare DNS over Namecheap
lines: Hit a strict limitation with a domain purchased on Namecheap: it wouldn't allow DNS records for both email forwarding and Resend configuration simultaneously.
The ultimate solution was migrating the domain's DNS hosting to Cloudflare.
Cloudflare handled the complex records effortlessly, allowing both Resend and email forwarding to coexist.

title: Asynchronous Event Processing
lines: I realized that for huge tasks, relying on simple HTTP requests would quickly overwhelm the system.
I had to stop treating the backend as just an HTTP response server.
Treating it as an asynchronous event-processing engine changed everything.

title: Strict Transactions
lines: I learned how dangerous it is to leave orphan data or incomplete records.
Now, I make sure to wrap every multi-step database operation in a transaction.
If it doesn't complete perfectly, the rollback saves everything.

title: Visual Hierarchy & Data-First Design
lines: I used to get caught up looking at beautiful sites and completely ignored their underlying structure.
I realized I need to deeply understand the kind of site I am building before styling it.
If it's a data-heavy site or a dashboard, perfecting the visual hierarchy and adopting a 'data-first design' approach is crucial.
